protocol: Structural no-go screen; no partial-copy optimizer was run after the pointwise NAND dominance proof.

proof.claim: Equal-grain g8 partial copies have no NAND-makespan advantage over some whole-expert opposite-group replication plan of no greater useful/page copy budget.
assumptions: 16 homogeneous healthy chips in two groups of eight
each expert has exactly one equal-size complete-row tile on every chip of its original group
all phase tiles have identical pages, waves and output row count
no tile is divided, copied weights remain immutable and every selected tile executes once
copy destinations arbitrary; multiple alternate copies are allowed and charged
integer waves and integral tile assignment, no fractional multiwave splitting
proof.construction: For each original group h independently, select a source j_h minimizing the number of distinct experts with any tile copy away from j_h. Replicate each such expert completely to the opposite group. If its set is S_h and C_h copies were stored for source group h, 8|S_h| <= C_h. Thus both group-wise useful bytes and physical pages of the new copy inventory are no greater.
proof.lower_bound: For every selected route, let n_h be the selected experts originally in group h and s_h the selected experts in S_h. The original partial plan cannot move the n_h-s_h mandatory jobs off source j_h, and must execute 8K total jobs. Its maximum per-chip tile count is at least L=max(ceil(K/2),n_0-s_0,n_1-s_1).
proof.achiever: Whole expert copies allow each selected copied expert to choose either group. Choose the group0 expert count in [n_0-s_0, K-(n_1-s_1)] nearest K/2. This is an integral assignment with maximum L on all eight chips/group. Exactly the same sets and proof work for every route, not only training routes.

cost_terms.NAND: Dominated pointwise; multiply tile count by its unchanged wave service.
cost_terms.output: Whole-group assignment gives exactly K tiles per channel-pair, hence minimum maximum channel output and the same mandatory PCIe output.
cost_terms.commands: Equal only when one native command is charged per original tile. Adjacent whole-row coalescing is a separate, legal controller operation.
cost_terms.host: Same selected experts, input/output tensors and GU->host activation->down barriers.
cost_terms.input: Full termwise dominance is false with same-expert input reuse after tile colocation. Counterexample supplied. The possible input gain is tiny here.

proof.capacity_qualification: The theorem covers useful bytes and pages, not arbitrary per-chip capacity caps or reserved block stripes. Whole copies can distribute copies differently and block rounding can change. A strong whole-copy baseline must be allowed to allocate its budget across layers and pack globally; imposing a fixed fraction in each layer can introduce artificial reservation losses.
proof.applicability: Does not cover unequal row sizes, heterogeneous chips, changing command granularity, online background, or a different pre-existing base placement.
proof.verdict: No-go for a new g8 partial-copy NAND balancing claim. Under one tile per native command, remaining gain is bounded by the input term. Do not claim a universal full-cost dominance theorem or no-go for row-run coalescing.

model_bounds.coalescing_bound_assumption: At least one native command per selected expert; no cross-expert row stacking/co-loading. This is not a universal bound once arbitrary command regrouping is permitted.
model_bounds.caveat: Only routed FFN service is modeled. Not full-model execution, not a quality experiment, not a 25/50% capacity-aware optimal solver. The full-copy oracle is mechanism headroom, not new partial-placement gain.

granite.native_interface: Each job is a whole-row shard. Optional coalescing only combines four adjacent copied output-row ranges of the same expert into one dense GEMV. No partial dot sums or weight changes.
granite.scope: This is a numerical structural counterexample, not a model route frequency or a learned layout. Unused model experts can retain their original one-copy placement.
granite.theorem_result: NAND dominance holds; full service termwise dominance fails if same-expert input reuse or adjacent-row command coalescing is allowed.
